long_synopsis: Week 74 brought consolidation rather than rupture. The Democracy Clock held at 8:14 p.m., not because pressure eased, but because advances in coercive and politicized governance were offset by limited judicial and local resistance. A new law poured roughly $70 billion into ICE, Border Patrol, and DHS without new accountability, while detainee protests, retaliatory detention findings, and opaque relocations exposed the human cost of an expanding enforcement system. In North Carolina, lawmakers and election officials advanced a coordinated package to tighten voting rules, shorten early voting, and increase partisan leverage over election administration. Meanwhile, public office was bent toward spectacle and gain through the White House-UFC nexus, redirected funds for a White House ballroom, and no-bid contracting. Courts blocked some abuses, restored public materials, and protected protest speech, but mostly acted defensively as discretion widened across institutions.
short_synopsis: The clock did not move, but the week deepened existing authoritarian lines: immigration enforcement expanded, dissent grew costlier, election rules tightened, and executive discretion spread through money, appointments, and spectacle.
